_comment: LED strip profiles for addressable (pixel) controllers.
An addressable strip needs two things set on its controller before it lights
correctly: the LIGHT BEAD SEQUENCE (which order it consumes its colour bytes
-- a GRB strip driven as RGB reads green-as-red) and the CHIP TYPE (its
driver IC). Both are printed on a reel or buried in a datasheet, and neither
is something a customer should have to look up. A profile is a named pair.
THE TWO ARE NOT INDEPENDENT. A four-letter sequence (RGBW, WBGR, ...) is a
four-channel pixel, and it is the CHIP TYPE that makes the controller send
four bytes per pixel instead of three. Pair a 4-letter sequence with a
3-channel chip and the byte stream misaligns, so the strip does not merely
show wrong colours -- part of it does not light at all. Observed on the
bench 2026-09-06: a strip on the defaults had its first 10 pixels dark and
coloured from pixel zero once set to WBGR + SK6812.
ONLY CONFIRMED PAIRS BELONG HERE. A plausible-looking sequence for a chip is
a guess, and a guess in this table sends somebody to the wrong setting with
our name on it. `chip_type: null` means we know the sequence but have never
confirmed the IC: writing the wrong IC changes the data protocol and the
strip stops working entirely, which is worse than asking once.
This file is the SINGLE source. The Nomad select builds its options from it
and publishes the resolved values as entity attributes, so the LED card
reads them from the entity rather than keeping a second copy.
The controller can be TOLD both: the Gledopto GL-SPI-206P / WZ-SPI exposes
`light_bead_sequence` (Tuya dp 101) and `chip_type` (dp 102) as settable

enums, so picking a profile writes them to the device. The vocabularies below are the CONVERTER's, not the hardware's: the WZ-SPI itself handles far more IC types (settable in the Tuya app or by RF remote), but Z2M's dp 102 lookup maps only ten. Values must come from
`bead_sequences` / `chip_types` below or Z2M silently drops the write.
Pixel count is NOT here: it depends how long a run the customer cut, not on
which strip it is, so it stays the device's own `lightpixel_number_set`
Adding a profile is a data change, no code.
`manufacturer_code` is what is printed on the reel or the datasheet, and is
how a customer will recognise their strip.
`id` is what the select STORES and what everything keys on. It never
changes. `name` is a LABEL: it is shown in the dropdown, it can be
shortened or re-worded freely, and nothing is stored against it. That
split is why the 2026-09-16 rename was a label edit rather than a fleet
migration. `aliases` carries any label a box may already have stored from
before the select moved to ids, so an old saved value still resolves; keep
an entry there when you re-word a name, and never reuse an id.

The label convention is `Product name (PRODUCT-CODE)`: the customer matches the CODE printed on the reel, and the name tells them they are in the right family. A dropdown of bare part numbers is hostile; bare names are ambiguous when a vendor ships several strips.

profiles.name: Standard
profiles.notes: No remap and no write. What every controller ships as, and the safe default for a correctly wired 3-channel strip.

profiles.name: LEDspace Splash Addressable RGB (SPLASH12T-SPI)
profiles.notes: GRB carried over from the card's original remap table, which is where this profile came from. The IC was never recorded, so it is left unset rather than guessed. Three-channel RGB.

profiles.name: LEDSpace RGBW 12mm (LINE12-PX-RGBW-24V)
profiles.notes: Confirmed working on the bench 2026-09-06: on the defaults the strip's first 10 pixels stayed dark; with WBGR + SK6812 it colours from pixel zero. Four-channel, white byte first, 24V, 36 px/m. The strip's actual IC is UCS2904. The WZ-SPI HARDWARE supports it (the controller handles ~49 IC types, settable in the Tuya app or by RF remote), but Z2M cannot select it: the converter's chip_type lookup on dp 102 maps only ten values and UCS2904 is not one. So SK6812 is a SUBSTITUTE forced by the CONVERTER, not by the controller, and it was found to be the best of the ten offered. Do not 'correct' it to UCS2904 while Z2M is the only way we set it.
